name: Agent navigates + edits (original)
what: Hazel's default coding agent, unchanged: one LLM uses Hazel's structured actions to build its own view (expand / collapse definitions) and make its own edits (update / insert / delete definitions); Hazel type-checks every edit. No Jev. Every other setup is compared against this one.

name: Jev picks first view, agent navigates + edits
short: Jev picks first view, agent navigates + edits
what: Before each user message reaches the agent, Jev (a fast, cheap yes/no model) looks at every definition and opens the ones relevant to the message. The agent still has expand and collapse and still writes every edit.
flow: Jev: relevant? one question per definition

name: Jev navigates, agent edits
what: The agent loses expand and collapse. To see code it describes what it needs in words (modify_view), and Jev decides which definitions to open. The agent still writes every edit itself. Called Mode 3 in Eval 002.

name: Agent sketches, Jev fills blanks
what: The agent loses its editing tools. It writes a sketch of the new code with ? holes, and Jev fills each hole by picking from the options Hazel says are type-correct. Kept as a baseline: the agent could often have typed the holes itself.
flow: Hazel lists typed options per hole

name: Agent specs, Jev builds code
what: Like the sketch mode, but the agent gives no code at all: only a path, an intent and the names it wants. Jev starts from a single hole and builds the whole shape (functions, conditionals, calls) one typed choice at a time.
flow: one hole; typed options incl. forms
Jev picks a form or a term

name: Jev navigates + builds, agent plans
what: Everything at once, as the UI's /jev-mode: Jev pre-selects the view, the agent can only navigate through Jev, and every edit is built by Jev from the agent's spec. The agent only plans.
flow: Jev builds, one typed pick at a time
